+def test_get_retry_after_ms_parses_http_date():
+    """Codex iter-1 finding #1 lock: get_retry_after_ms must parse the
+    HTTP-date format used in Retry-After headers (case-insensitive
+    header matching).
+    """
+    import time
+    from email.utils import format_datetime
+    from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
+    from core import get_retry_after_ms
+
+    # Future date: ~10 seconds from now.
+    future = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=10)
+    http_date = format_datetime(future)  # produces "Wed, ... GMT"
+
+    out = get_retry_after_ms(f"HTTP 429: Retry-After: {http_date}")
+    # Should return ~10000ms (allow some slack).
+    assert 5000 <= out <= 15000, (
+        f"HTTP-date Retry-After parsing failed; got {out}ms, "
+        f"expected ~10000ms (Codex iter-1 #1)"
+    )
+
+    # Lower-case header name still works (RFC says case-insensitive).
+    out_lower = get_retry_after_ms(f"retry-after: {http_date}")
+    assert 5000 <= out_lower <= 15000
+
+

+    """Codex iter-1 finding #2 lock: extract_nested_error_message must
+    walk nested .error.message and .error.error.message JSON paths
+    (the shape Bedrock + Anthropic API actually return).

+    import json as _json

+    )
+    out1 = extract_nested_error_message(body1)
+    assert "AccessDenied" in out1, (
+        f"single-nested .error.message must be extracted; got {out1!r}"

 203:         try:
 204:             dt = parsedate_to_datetime(m.group(1))
 205:             wait = max(0, int((dt.timestamp() - time.time()) * 1000))
 206:             return wait
 207:         except (ValueError, TypeError):
 208:             return 0
 209:     return 0
 210: 
 211: 
 212: class ErrorClassifier:
 213:     """Classifies Bedrock exceptions into a (category, recovery, debug_msg) triple.
 214: 
 215:     Verbatim port of v4's classifier. Recovery values:
 216:       - "strip_cache_retry": cache_control rejected; strip blocks and retry once
 217:       - "compact_retry":     prompt-too-long; caller should compact and retry
 218:       - "backoff":           transient (throttle/503/network); retry with jitter
 219:       - "no_retry":          permanent (validation/access denied); surface to user
 220:     """
 221: 
 222:     @staticmethod
 223:     def classify(exc: Exception):
 224:         msg_lower = str(exc).lower()
 225:         cls_name = type(exc).__name__.lower()
 226: 
 227:         # Block L additions â€” check most-specific first.
 228:         if "max_tokens" in msg_lower or "max output tokens" in msg_lower or "output token limit" in msg_lower:
 229:             return BedrockErrorCategory.MAX_TOKENS_OVERFLOW, "compact_retry", str(exc)[:200]
 230:         if "<html" in msg_lower or "<body" in msg_lower or "<title" in msg_lower:
 231:             # Raw HTML 5xx error â€” backoff + humanize before user-facing display.
 232:             return BedrockErrorCategory.BEDROCK_5XX_HTML, "backoff", str(exc)[:200]
 233:         if "504" in msg_lower or "gatewaytimeout" in msg_lower:
 234:             return BedrockErrorCategory.GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, "backoff", str(exc)[:200]
 235:         if "413" in msg_lower or "payload too large" in msg_lower or "request entity too large" in msg_lower:
 236:             return BedrockErrorCategory.PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "compact_retry", str(exc)[:200]
 237:         if "409" in msg_lower or "conflictexception" in msg_lower:
 238:             return BedrockErrorCategory.CONFLICT_409, "no_retry", str(exc)[:200]
 239:         # Codex iter-1 finding #3: broaden timeout matching to common shapes
 240:         # ReadTimeout / ConnectTimeout / APIConnectionTimeoutError / "timed out".
 241:         # Note: Phase 8 NETWORK pattern still catches connect/read timeouts
 242:         # as cls_name matches; this REQUEST_TIMEOUT branch must run BEFORE
 243:         # the NETWORK branch to differentiate them. Both are retryable.
 244:         if (
 245:             "request_timeout" in msg_lower
 246:             or "request-timeout" in msg_lower
 247:             or "408" in msg_lower
 248:             or "request timed out" in msg_lower
 249:             or "timed out" in msg_lower
 250:             or "timeout" in cls_name
 251:             or "apiconnectiontimeout" in cls_name
 252:         ):
 253:             return BedrockErrorCategory.REQUEST_TIMEOUT, "backoff", str(exc)[:200]
 254:         if "malformed" in msg_lower or "could not parse response" in msg_lower or "decode" in cls_name:
 255:             return BedrockErrorCategory.MALFORMED_RESPONSE, "backoff", str(exc)[:200]
 256:         if "sigv4" in msg_lower or "signature" in msg_lower or "credentialverify" in cls_name:
 257:             return BedrockErrorCategory.SIGV4_FAILURE, "no_retry", str(exc)[:200]
 258:         if "dependency" in msg_lower or "dependencyfailedexception" in msg_lower:
 259:             return BedrockErrorCategory.DEPENDENCY_FAILURE, "backoff", str(exc)[:200]

+# ============================================================
+# Codex iter-1 finding-lock tests
+# ============================================================
+
+def test_get_retry_after_ms_parses_http_date():
+    """Codex iter-1 finding #1 lock: get_retry_after_ms must parse the
+    HTTP-date format used in Retry-After headers (case-insensitive
+    header matching).
+    """
+    import time
+    from email.utils import format_datetime
+    from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
+    from core import get_retry_after_ms
+
+    # Future date: ~10 seconds from now.
+    future = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=10)
+    http_date = format_datetime(future)  # produces "Wed, ... GMT"
+
+    out = get_retry_after_ms(f"HTTP 429: Retry-After: {http_date}")
+    # Should return ~10000ms (allow some slack).
+    assert 5000 <= out <= 15000, (
+        f"HTTP-date Retry-After parsing failed; got {out}ms, "
+        f"expected ~10000ms (Codex iter-1 #1)"
+    )
+
+    # Lower-case header name still works (RFC says case-insensitive).
+    out_lower = get_retry_after_ms(f"retry-after: {http_date}")
+    assert 5000 <= out_lower <= 15000
+
+
+def test_extract_nested_error_message_extracts_nested_api_json():
+    """Codex iter-1 finding #2 lock: extract_nested_error_message must
+    walk nested .error.message and .error.error.message JSON paths
+    (the shape Bedrock + Anthropic API actually return).
+    """
+    import json as _json
+    from core import extract_nested_error_message
+
+    # Single-nested .error.message.
+    body1 = _json.dumps(
+        {"error": {"message": "AccessDenied: principal lacks permission"}}
+    )
+    out1 = extract_nested_error_message(body1)
+    assert "AccessDenied" in out1, (
+        f"single-nested .error.message must be extracted; got {out1!r}"
+    )
+
+    # Double-nested .error.error.message.
+    body2 = _json.dumps(
+        {"error": {"error": {"message": "ThrottlingException: rate exceeded"}}}
+    )
+    out2 = extract_nested_error_message(body2)
+    assert "ThrottlingException" in out2, (
+        f"double-nested .error.error.message must be extracted; got {out2!r}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_classifier_recognizes_common_timeout_shapes():
+    """Codex iter-1 finding #3 lock: classifier must catch common
+    timeout exception shapes (ReadTimeout, ConnectTimeout,
+    APIConnectionTimeoutError, "request timed out").
+    """
+    from core import BedrockErrorCategory, ErrorClassifier
+
+    # Class-name shapes (cls_name match).
+    class ReadTimeout(Exception):
+        pass
+
+    class ConnectTimeout(Exception):
+        pass
+
+    class APIConnectionTimeoutError(Exception):
+        pass
+
+    cases = [
+        ReadTimeout("read timed out"),
+        ConnectTimeout("connect timed out"),
+        APIConnectionTimeoutError("connection timeout"),
+        Exception("Request timed out after 30s"),
+    ]
+    for exc in cases:
+        cat, recovery, _ = ErrorClassifier.classify(exc)
+        assert cat == BedrockErrorCategory.REQUEST_TIMEOUT, (
+            f"{type(exc).__name__}({exc!r}) → got {cat}, "
+            f"expected REQUEST_TIMEOUT (Codex iter-1 #3)"
+        )
+        assert recovery == "backoff"
+
+

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:175:## ADR-005 — BedrockClient: REUSE v4 verbatim (Bedrock-native), defer Runnable cache-break detection to Phase 6
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:185:N/A — replacement, not addition. v4's BedrockClient is already Bedrock-native, has prompt cache fallback, retry classifier, mock mode, thinking mode. Runnable's `claude.ts` is Anthropic-direct (subscriber/OAuth flows), not applicable to Bedrock.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:198:### Why NOT port Runnable's `promptCacheBreakDetection.ts` here
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:199:Runnable's detection is sophisticated (systemHash + toolsHash + perToolHashes + cacheControlHash + globalCacheStrategy + betas list etc.) and depends on having multi-block system prompt + cache-control state. v5 doesn't have multi-block prompts until Phase 6 lands. Porting now would build a detector against a structure that doesn't exist yet, causing rework.

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:204:N/A for ADR-005 itself (no Runnable code adopted yet). Phase 6 ADR will track the cache-break-detection port.

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:342:- Runnable's `permissionContext` (a complex `DeepImmutable` of allow/deny/ask rules + plan-mode + bypass mode + MCP server-prefix rules) is REPLACED with a simpler `(plan_mode: bool, deny_rules: set[str] | None)` pair.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:343:- Justification: Runnable's permission context exists because the Anthropic-direct CLI has multi-source rules (user config, project config, settings, MCP server scopes). v5's Bedrock-only `.ipynb` has none of those sources — approval is a single ipywidgets prompt per call. Constraint = **`.ipynb`** (single approval source).
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:344:- Up-stream caller: Phase 8's `core/query_engine.py` calls `get_tools(plan_mode=ctx.plan_mode)` per turn (mirrors Runnable's `claude.ts` calling `getTools(permissionContext)` per request).
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:345:- Down-stream wiring: tools' `requires_approval` flag drives the ipywidgets approval prompt; v5 does NOT call Runnable's `checkPermissions()` (which returns a structured `PermissionResult`) because there's no permission context to check against. Instead, `requires_approval=True` triggers the user prompt directly. Documented as a v4-native ADAPT, not drift.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:346:- Error contract: tool execution errors propagate as raised exceptions; `core/query_engine.py` (Phase 8) maps to `tool_result` blocks. Runnable's pattern is identical.

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:444:**Why diff_widget.py:** PS_actual_use_problems.md captures a real pattern where v4 users approved edits without seeing the actual change content, then discovered later that the model had edited the wrong region or stripped useful code. Showing the colored diff inline (with ±3 lines context) lets the user catch misplaced edits BEFORE clicking Approve. Runnable solved this with `EditTool/UI.tsx` (Ink JSX). v5 ipywidgets equivalent: an HTML widget with `+` green / `-` red / context gray + a `<details>` block for click-to-expand-full-file.

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:596:The PS Issue #7 root cause: v4 grew the system prompt by *appending* — every Hermes pattern, Runnable adoption, Learning_Factory pattern, and v4-original addition was concatenated to the f-string. compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:686:## ADR-013 — Phase 7 ToolSearchTool deferred loading (highest-leverage Runnable port)
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:691:  - Runnable: `gg-claude-code-runnable/src/tools/ToolSearchTool/ToolSearchTool.ts` (471 LOC) + `prompt.ts` (121 LOC) + `constants.ts`
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:692:  - Runnable: `gg-claude-code-runnable/src/utils/toolSearch.ts` (deferred-tool placement logic)
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:702:**Why tool_search.py:** the v4 system loads every tool's full JSON schema on every turn. With 30 tools that's ~5000-8000 tokens of schema in EVERY message — pure overhead since the model uses ~3-5 tools per turn. Runnable's deferred-loading pattern: low-frequency tool schemas are NOT in the initial prompt; instead, only their NAMES appear in a `<system-reminder>`. When the model needs one, it calls `tool_search("name")` which returns the full schema in a `<functions>` block, after which the tool is callable like any other.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:704:This is the **single highest-leverage token-saving Runnable adoption** in v5 — V5_PLAN.md targets ≥3000 tokens/turn savings.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:96:Four read-only tools land per ADR-001 (file-per-tool) + ADR-009 (REUSE v4 executor + ADAPT Runnable prompt). Multiple functional improvements vs v4:
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:99:- **v4 prompt**: v4 didn't make a Runnable-style claim about ripgrep (its description says "regex search").
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:100:- **Runnable prompt**: claims "built on ripgrep" (true for Runnable's TS version which embeds ripgrep in the bun binary).
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:102:- **Why this is "better than Runnable"**: v5's prompt is *honest* about the backend. Runnable's prompt would mislead the model in v5 because v5 doesn't have ripgrep. Pattern syntax differs (ripgrep PCRE2 vs Python re) and the model would write the wrong escapes if it believed the prompt. PS Issue #6 (wiring-bug pattern) prevention.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:110:### 3.3 list_dir — kept dedicated tool against Runnable's "use bash ls" advice
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:111:- **Runnable prompt for read_file**: "This tool can only read files, not directories. To read a directory, use an `ls` command via the Bash tool."
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:116:- **Better than Runnable**: v5 plan-mode users can fully navigate the workspace without bash. Runnable plan-mode users cannot.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:131:- **v5**: all 4 read-only tools declare `is_concurrency_safe=True` (Runnable parity). When Phase 9's Task tool dispatches multiple read-only tool calls in parallel, the registry will allow batching.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:143:- **Behavior delta**: misplaced edits are catchable at approval time. **Better than v4 AND Runnable**: Runnable's UI.tsx Ink renderer was the inspiration; v5 brings the same UX to ipynb where v4 had only a text summary. (Runnable is not "better" here — they had this; v4 didn't; v5 catches up + integrates with .ipynb.)
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:161:### 4.5 view_image is read-only with no Runnable analog
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:162:- **Runnable** integrates image reading into FileReadTool — model just calls `read_file("img.png")` and the tool detects the format and returns base64 inline.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:164:- **Better than Runnable**: clearer audit trail. Not "better" technically — it's a stylistic v4-parity choice that makes audits easier.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:237:- **Better than v4 (and Runnable)**: this specific failure mode doesn't exist in Runnable's prompt (Runnable doesn't have a `max_exec_calls_per_session` constraint). v5 inherits the constraint from v4 but fixes the prompt-engineering failure that v4.10.10 patched ineffectually.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:246:- **v4**: no token caps. Each Hermes/Runnable/LF integration appended to the f-string; reviewers signed off individually but nobody reviewed the aggregate. Result: 914 LOC of unreviewable content.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:255:- **Better than v4 + Runnable**: Runnable has the equivalent (`promptCacheBreakDetection.ts`) but Phase 6 keeps the v5 implementation focused (just enough for Phase 6's needs); Phase 12+ may extend with per-tool hashes when those concerns arrive.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:270:The single highest-leverage token-saving Runnable adoption. v4 ships every tool's full schema on every turn — pure overhead, since the model uses ~3-5 tools per turn out of ~10-30. Phase 7 ports Runnable's deferred-loading pattern: low-frequency tool schemas are NOT in the per-turn prompt; only their names appear in a `<system-reminder>`. When the model needs one, it calls `tool_search("<query>")` which returns the full schema in a `<functions>` block.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:279:- **Runnable parity**: drops feature-gate branches (FORK_SUBAGENT / KAIROS / GrowthBook) that are Anthropic-internal. Drops async/Promise compute (v5 sync, static descriptions). Drops lodash memoize (overkill for static).
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:299:- Runnable's wire format: each matched tool appears as one `<function>{"description":..., "name":..., "parameters":...}</function>` line inside a `<functions>` block. Bedrock and Anthropic API both treat anything inside `<functions>` as additional callable tools.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:337:- **Per-tool result truncation**: tool_result is truncated to each tool's `max_result_size_chars` (Runnable parity). v4 used a single global cap.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:386:- **Parallel sub-agent dispatch**: deferred. Runnable does it via async generators; v5 .ipynb is sync.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:77:- **Adapted**: Runnable's complex `DeepImmutable PermissionContext` (multi-source rules: user config / project config / settings / MCP scopes / plan-mode / bypass mode) collapsed into v5's `(plan_mode: bool, deny_rules: set[str] | None)` tuple. Reason: v5's `.ipynb` has a SINGLE approval source (ipywidgets prompt per call). Runnable's multi-source surface doesn't apply. Constraint = `.ipynb`.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:78:- **Better than Runnable**: v5's registry **rejects duplicate registrations** with a loud `ValueError`. Runnable allows tool authors to override existing entries silently — real bug source in v4 where two skills both registered `verify` and the second won. Locked by `test_register_duplicate_name_raises`.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:79:- **Better than Runnable**: v5's `assemble_tool_pool(plan_mode=True)` enforces the allowlist on MCP tools at registry-assembly time. v4 enforced at dispatch time, which let the model see the disallowed tool schema in the initial prompt. v5 hides them entirely.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:90:### From Runnable: FileReadTool prompt structure (PORT_LOG #003)
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:93:- **What we kept**: Runnable's WHEN/WHEN NOT structure — explicitly listing when the tool IS the right choice and when it's NOT. This addresses PS Issue #7 (buried-matrix failure mode in v4 where the tool list was a flat bullet list with no triage guidance, and the model under-attended to mid-list bullets). Each v5 read-only tool description ends with WHEN/WHEN NOT.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:94:- **What we adapted**: tool naming. v4 uses `read_file`, Runnable uses `Read`. v5 keeps `read_file` to avoid confusing the model with the English verb "read".
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:96:### From Runnable: GrepTool prompt with critical correction (PORT_LOG #004)
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:97:- **Source**: `gg-claude-code-runnable/src/tools/GrepTool/prompt.ts`. The Runnable text says `"A powerful search tool built on ripgrep"`.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:99:- **Why we corrected**: v5 (and v4) implement grep with Python's `re` module — there is no ripgrep binary in the runtime. If we'd kept Runnable's text verbatim, the model would write ripgrep PCRE2 patterns (e.g., `(?P<name>...)` works but `(?P_name_...)` doesn't, ripgrep extensions like `[[:alpha:]]` don't behave identically to Python's). PS Issue #6 (wiring-bug pattern: tool description claims behavior the executor doesn't implement) — the exact failure mode v5 is meant to prevent.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:100:- **Better than Runnable**: v5 grep prompt is *implementation-truthful*. Runnable's prompt would be wrong in v5's environment.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:106:- **Better than Runnable**: v5 glob can find files in adjacent project dirs without the model needing to know about the allowed_paths feature.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:111:- **Better than Runnable**: v5 plan-mode users can navigate the workspace fully. Runnable plan-mode users cannot.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:126:- **What we dropped**: Runnable's "NEVER create *.md / README files unless explicitly requested" + "no emojis" rules. Each individual integration was reviewed; the aggregate failed.

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0-iter2.md:2074:  - Runnable: `gg-claude-code-runnable/src/tools/ToolSearchTool/ToolSearchTool.ts` (471 LOC) + `prompt.ts` (121 LOC) + `constants.ts`

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0-iter2.md:2085:**Why tool_search.py:** the v4 system loads every tool's full JSON schema on every turn. With 30 tools that's ~5000-8000 tokens of schema in EVERY message â€” pure overhead since the model uses ~3-5 tools per turn. Runnable's deferred-loading pattern: low-frequency tool schemas are NOT in the initial prompt; instead, only their NAMES appear in a `<system-reminder>`. When the model needs one, it calls `tool_search("name")` which returns the full schema in a `<functions>` block, after which the tool is callable like any other.
compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0-iter2.md:2087:This is the **single highest-leverage token-saving Runnable adoption** in v5 â€” V5_PLAN.md targets â‰¥3000 tokens/turn savings.

Each individual integration was reviewed; the aggregate failed.
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW.md:646:Round 3 fixes (8 in-place changes) addressed the immediate failure but **could not address the structural cause** without an architectural refactor. compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0.md:2085:**Why tool_search.py:** the v4 system loads every tool's full JSON schema on every turn. With 30 tools that's ~5000-8000 tokens of schema in EVERY message â€” pure overhead since the model uses ~3-5 tools per turn. Runnable's deferred-loading pattern: low-frequency tool schemas are NOT in the initial prompt; instead, only their NAMES appear in a `<system-reminder>`. When the model needs one, it calls `tool_search("name")` which returns the full schema in a `<functions>` block, after which the tool is callable like any other.
compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0.md:2087:This is the **single highest-leverage token-saving Runnable adoption** in v5 â€” V5_PLAN.md targets â‰¥3000 tokens/turn savings.

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:948:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\v3_architecture.html:215:    <p class="subtitle">A secure AI coding assistant that runs inside AWS SageMaker notebooks. It reads your code, writes files, edits Jupyter notebooks surgically, creates documents, generates charts, and helps you build software &mdash; all through a chat interface. v4.10.0 shipped 5 Runnable-parity upgrades. v4.10.1 added Context Collapse + Sonnet 4.5 default. v4.10.2 softened the verify-contract. v4.10.3 added ship-gate verifier + cache-boundary regression test + many-skill stress test + clearer permission denials. v4.10.4 closed the largest remaining gap: sub-agents now receive a bounded work-context handoff block (AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + recent changed files) on top of v4.10.0's env-details. v4.10.5 adopted 3 Learning_Factory prompt-only patterns: post-compact resume protocol, structured summary sections, skill self-patching 4-rule check. v4.10.6 added the html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables, with screenshot-iteration loop. v4.10.7 hardened destructive-command coverage: ~50 new bash patterns + ~12 python patterns spanning cloud / IaC / orchestration / storage / DB CLI / persistence / system-overwrite, HIGH_RISK_TOOLS excluded from Always-Approve UI, cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks. v4.10.8 closed the residual obfuscation escape route (base64/xxd/eval pipe-to-shell now blocked across more interpreters) and hard-blocked recursive folder removal from the agent (`rm -r/-rf/-fr/-R/--recursive`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `shutil.rmtree`, `os.rmdir`, `os.removedirs`, `Path(...).rmdir()`) â€” single-file cleanup still allowed; the ðŸ§¹ Clean button still works in-process. v4.10.9 closed Codex's third local-hook finding by adding a narrow backtick eval+downloader pattern (defense-in-depth only â€” eval was already excluded from the bash allowlist; zero new false-positive risk). v4.10.10 surfaced the previously-hardcoded `aws_bedrock_only` setting as a UI checkbox in cell 2 of `chat.ipynb` (default ticked = strict). Codex review on v4.10.10: PASS. 134/134 destructive-coverage tests + 122 v4 unit tests + 16/16 hook obfuscation self-test all green.</p>

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1208:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:741:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable targets Anthropic's direct API. Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1212:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1218:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop â€” that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1219:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:903:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:10px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> These aren't cosmetic changes. Each gap represented a behavioral regression vs Runnable that only showed up under specific conditions. For example, Gap #4 only surfaces during long sessions with many small tasks â€” exactly the scenario where users most need automatic quality gates. Together, these 7 fixes close the last measurable quality delta between V4 and Runnable on prompt engineering. <b>Remaining differences are infrastructure (ink TUI, remote sessions, voice), not agentic quality.</b></p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1221:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:970:      <p>Because the environment is different. Runnable is a CLI product built for Anthropic's own stack and a terminal-first workflow. V4 is optimized for SageMaker, notebooks, Bedrock pricing, and a user who often wants reports and visible widgets, not only terminal throughput.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1225:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:1062:      <tr><td>Is V4 fully identical to runnable?</td><td>~99%. Only remaining difference: Runnable has remote review sessions (ultrareview/CCR cloud infrastructure) â€” not applicable to SageMaker. See <code>compact_v4/docs/V4_6_RUNNABLE_UPGRADE.md</code>.</td></tr>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1226:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:1063:      <tr><td>Is V4 better than Runnable for SageMaker?</td><td>Yes. compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1418:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT_v4.html:105:  Why is <strong>Hermes</strong> (self-improving agent) different from <strong>Runnable / SageMaker V4</strong> (coding agent)?<br>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1422:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT_v4.html:245:    <strong>Key insight:</strong> Runnable and V4 are <em>task runners</em>. They do one job well, then stop. Hermes is a <em>persistent companion</em> that accumulates knowledge. Oracle needs to become the Hermes equivalent for sales â€” learning from each call and improving its next decision.

V4.6.1 matches Runnable's review/verification quality AND has SageMaker-specific features: budget slider with soft-stop, cache savings display, diminishing returns detection, document generation (Word/Excel/PDF/charts), 16 security layers with AST validation, Bedrock-native prompt caching, and 9 specialized skills (including new simplify, security-review).</td></tr>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1973:.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\phase-09.md:1101:compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:215:    <p class="subtitle">A secure AI coding assistant that runs inside AWS SageMaker notebooks. It reads your code, writes files, edits Jupyter notebooks surgically, creates documents, generates charts, and helps you build software &mdash; all through a chat interface. v4.10.0 shipped 5 Runnable-parity upgrades. v4.10.1 added Context Collapse + Sonnet 4.5 default. v4.10.2 softened the verify-contract. v4.10.3 added ship-gate verifier + cache-boundary regression test + many-skill stress test + clearer permission denials. v4.10.4 closed the largest remaining gap: sub-agents now receive a bounded work-context handoff block (AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + recent changed files) on top of v4.10.0's env-details. v4.10.5 adopted 3 Learning_Factory prompt-only patterns: post-compact resume protocol, structured summary sections, skill self-patching 4-rule check. v4.10.6 added the html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables, with screenshot-iteration loop. v4.10.7 hardened destructive-command coverage: ~50 new bash patterns + ~12 python patterns spanning cloud / IaC / orchestration / storage / DB CLI / persistence / system-overwrite, HIGH_RISK_TOOLS excluded from Always-Approve UI, cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks. v4.10.8 closed the residual obfuscation escape route (base64/xxd/eval pipe-to-shell now blocked across more interpreters) and hard-blocked recursive folder removal from the agent (`rm -r/-rf/-fr/-R/--recursive`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `shutil.rmtree`, `os.rmdir`, `os.removedirs`, `Path(...).rmdir()`) â€” single-file cleanup still allowed; the ðŸ§¹ Clean button still works in-process. v4.10.9 closed Codex's third local-hook finding by adding a narrow backtick eval+downloader pattern (defense-in-depth only â€” eval was already excluded from the bash allowlist; zero new false-positive risk). v4.10.10 surfaced the previously-hardcoded `aws_bedrock_only` setting as a UI checkbox in cell 2 of `chat.ipynb` (default ticked = strict). Codex review on v4.10.10: PASS. 134/134 destructive-coverage tests + 122 v4 unit tests + 16/16 hook obfuscation self-test all green.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2349:.\compact_v5\_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets â€” set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 â€” `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 â€” `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 â€” minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 â€” prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 â€” IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 â€” opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 â€” production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 â€” `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 â€” Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 â€” same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 â€” verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 â€” production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 â€” sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 â€” Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 â€” html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 â€” destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 â€” obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 â€” backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only â€” `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** â€” `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes â€” all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders â€” `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2870:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\tabbed_design.html:101:  Why is <strong>Hermes</strong> (self-improving agent) different from <strong>Runnable / SageMaker V4</strong> (coding agent)?<br>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2874:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\tabbed_design.html:241:    <strong>Key insight:</strong> Runnable and V4 are <em>task runners</em>. They do one job well, then stop. Hermes is a <em>persistent companion</em> that accumulates knowledge. Oracle needs to become the Hermes equivalent for sales â€” learning from each call and improving its next decision.
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2875:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\tabbed_design.html:255:  <p class="desc">Left = what Runnable and SageMaker V4 do every session. Right = what Hermes does on top of that. The core loop is identical â€” the difference is what happens AFTER the response.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2917:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:741:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable targets Anthropic's direct API. Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2921:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2927:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop â€” that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2928:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:903:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:10px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> These aren't cosmetic changes. Each gap represented a behavioral regression vs Runnable that only showed up under specific conditions. For example, Gap #4 only surfaces during long sessions with many small tasks â€” exactly the scenario where users most need automatic quality gates. Together, these 7 fixes close the last measurable quality delta between V4 and Runnable on prompt engineering. <b>Remaining differences are infrastructure (ink TUI, remote sessions, voice), not agentic quality.</b></p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2930:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:970:      <p>Because the environment is different. Runnable is a CLI product built for Anthropic's own stack and a terminal-first workflow. V4 is optimized for SageMaker, notebooks, Bedrock pricing, and a user who often wants reports and visible widgets, not only terminal throughput.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2934:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:1062:      <tr><td>Is V4 fully identical to runnable?</td><td>~99%. All 7 gaps from deep audit closed: verification contract, USE WHEN guidance, FP filtering, auto-nudge, critical reminder, fork semantics, skill discovery auto-surfacing. Only remaining difference: Runnable has remote review sessions (ultrareview/CCR cloud infrastructure) â€” not applicable to SageMaker. See <code>compact_v4/docs/V4_6_RUNNABLE_UPGRADE.md</code>.</td></tr>

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3186:.\SESSION_STATE.md:738:5. **#41a Reactive Compact on CONTEXT_OVERFLOW** â€” when Bedrock rejects with "prompt is too long" / "too many tokens" / "input is too long", agent runs microcompact (or placeholder-summary fallback if microcompact freed less than `MICROCOMPACT_MIN_SAVINGS` â€” deliberately NO additional LLM call), clears file-read state, sets `_cache_broken_by_compact` (both branches), and retries the same request once. compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4725:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT.html:89:  Why is <strong>Hermes</strong> (self-improving agent) different from <strong>Runnable / SageMaker V4</strong> (coding agent)?<br>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4729:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT.html:229:    <strong>Key insight:</strong> Runnable and V4 are <em>task runners</em>. They do one job well, then stop. Hermes is a <em>persistent companion</em> that accumulates knowledge. Oracle needs to become the Hermes equivalent for sales â€” learning from each call and improving its next decision.
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4730:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT.html:243:  <p class="desc">Left = what Runnable and SageMaker V4 do every session. Right = what Hermes does on top of that. The core loop is identical â€” the difference is what happens AFTER the response.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4814:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:741:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable targets Anthropic's direct API. Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4818:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4824:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop â€” that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4825:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:903:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:10px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> These aren't cosmetic changes. Each gap represented a behavioral regression vs Runnable that only showed up under specific conditions. For example, Gap #4 only surfaces during long sessions with many small tasks â€” exactly the scenario where users most need automatic quality gates. Together, these 7 fixes close the last measurable quality delta between V4 and Runnable on prompt engineering. <b>Remaining differences are infrastructure (ink TUI, remote sessions, voice), not agentic quality.</b></p>

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:6185:   `has_thinking_blocks()` is ported, but [bedrock_client.py](/abs/path/D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/runtime/bedrock_client.py:408) always sends `max_tokens: 1` and never adds `thinking`. Runnable’s CountTokens path switches to `max_tokens=2048` and includes `thinking` when prior messages contain thinking blocks. This can fail or undercount exactly the R4 #43 case the helper was added for. The raw call shape itself is otherwise aligned with AWS CountTokens docs: `modelId` plus `input.invokeModel.body`.

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:590:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW.md:644:The 5-investigator deep dive (Team A1 prompt-engineering, A2 tool-design, B1 session forensics, B2 Hermes/Runnable comparative, Codex deep architectural) identified the root cause as **aggregate prompt growth from multi-source integration** (Hermes patterns + Runnable patterns + Learning_Factory patterns + v4-original additions = ~5000+ static tokens). compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1261:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:948:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\v3_architecture.html:215:    <p class="subtitle">A secure AI coding assistant that runs inside AWS SageMaker notebooks. It reads your code, writes files, edits Jupyter notebooks surgically, creates documents, generates charts, and helps you build software &mdash; all through a chat interface. v4.10.0 shipped 5 Runnable-parity upgrades. v4.10.1 added Context Collapse + Sonnet 4.5 default. v4.10.2 softened the verify-contract. v4.10.3 added ship-gate verifier + cache-boundary regression test + many-skill stress test + clearer permission denials. v4.10.4 closed the largest remaining gap: sub-agents now receive a bounded work-context handoff block (AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + recent changed files) on top of v4.10.0's env-details. v4.10.5 adopted 3 Learning_Factory prompt-only patterns: post-compact resume protocol, structured summary sections, skill self-patching 4-rule check. v4.10.6 added the html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables, with screenshot-iteration loop. v4.10.7 hardened destructive-command coverage: ~50 new bash patterns + ~12 python patterns spanning cloud / IaC / orchestration / storage / DB CLI / persistence / system-overwrite, HIGH_RISK_TOOLS excluded from Always-Approve UI, cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks. v4.10.8 closed the residual obfuscation escape route (base64/xxd/eval pipe-to-shell now blocked across more interpreters) and hard-blocked recursive folder removal from the agent (`rm -r/-rf/-fr/-R/--recursive`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `shutil.rmtree`, `os.rmdir`, `os.removedirs`, `Path(...).rmdir()`) Ã¢â‚¬â€ single-file cleanup still allowed; the Ã°Å¸Â§Â¹ Clean button still works in-process. v4.10.9 closed Codex's third local-hook finding by adding a narrow backtick eval+downloader pattern (defense-in-depth only Ã¢â‚¬â€ eval was already excluded from the bash allowlist; zero new false-positive risk). v4.10.10 surfaced the previously-hardcoded `aws_bedrock_only` setting as a UI checkbox in cell 2 of `chat.ipynb` (default ticked = strict). Codex review on v4.10.10: PASS. 134/134 destructive-coverage tests + 122 v4 unit tests + 16/16 hook obfuscation self-test all green.</p>

Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1276:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1212:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1277:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1218:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop Ã¢â‚¬â€ that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1278:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1219:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:903:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:10px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> These aren't cosmetic changes. Each gap represented a behavioral regression vs Runnable that only showed up under specific conditions. For example, Gap #4 only surfaces during long sessions with many small tasks Ã¢â‚¬â€ exactly the scenario where users most need automatic quality gates. Together, these 7 fixes close the last measurable quality delta between V4 and Runnable on prompt engineering. <b>Remaining differences are infrastructure (ink TUI, remote sessions, voice), not agentic quality.</b></p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1279:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1221:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:970:      <p>Because the environment is different. Runnable is a CLI product built for Anthropic's own stack and a terminal-first workflow. V4 is optimized for SageMaker, notebooks, Bedrock pricing, and a user who often wants reports and visible widgets, not only terminal throughput.</p>

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1296:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:1422:.\compact_v5\docs\htmls\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT_v4.html:245:    <strong>Key insight:</strong> Runnable and V4 are <em>task runners</em>. Oracle needs to become the Hermes equivalent for sales Ã¢â‚¬â€ learning from each call and improving its next decision.

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1336:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2917:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:741:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable targets Anthropic's direct API. Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1337:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2921:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1338:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2927:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop Ã¢â‚¬â€ that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1339:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2928:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:903:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:10px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> These aren't cosmetic changes. Each gap represented a behavioral regression vs Runnable that only showed up under specific conditions. For example, Gap #4 only surfaces during long sessions with many small tasks Ã¢â‚¬â€ exactly the scenario where users most need automatic quality gates. Together, these 7 fixes close the last measurable quality delta between V4 and Runnable on prompt engineering. <b>Remaining differences are infrastructure (ink TUI, remote sessions, voice), not agentic quality.</b></p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1340:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2930:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:970:      <p>Because the environment is different. Runnable is a CLI product built for Anthropic's own stack and a terminal-first workflow. V4 is optimized for SageMaker, notebooks, Bedrock pricing, and a user who often wants reports and visible widgets, not only terminal throughput.</p>

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1412:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4729:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT.html:229:    <strong>Key insight:</strong> Runnable and V4 are <em>task runners</em>. Oracle needs to become the Hermes equivalent for sales Ã¢â‚¬â€ learning from each call and improving its next decision.

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1414:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4814:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:741:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable targets Anthropic's direct API. Bedrock has different validation rules, pricing, and caching behavior. V4 handles these differences natively so you don't hit surprise errors or pay more than necessary.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1415:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4818:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:759:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Runnable outputs code diffs for developers. V4 outputs reports, charts, and documents for business users who need deliverables they can share with stakeholders, not just code changes.</p>
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1416:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4824:.\PS_ClaudeCode_Insights\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop Ã¢â‚¬â€ that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
